{{Elections in Vermont}}
The '''2022 United States House of Representatives election in Vermont''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect the [[U.S. representative]] from {{ushr|VT|AL}}. The election will coincide with [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2022 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]], as well as various other [[2022 United States elections|state and local elections]].

Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] [[Peter Welch]] was re-elected with 67.3% of the vote in [[2020 United States House of Representatives election in Vermont|2020]]. After eight-term U.S. Senator [[Patrick Leahy]] announced he would retire on November 15, some speculated that Welch may decline to seek re-election and instead seek election to the Senate.<ref>{{cite web|last=Allison|first=Natalie|title=Leahy, most senior senator, will retire|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2021/11/15/leahy-most-senior-senator-will-retire-522356|access-date=2021-11-16|website=POLITICO|language=en|date=November 15, 2021}}</ref> On November 22, 2021, Welch announced his candidacy for Leahy's seat, creating the first open U.S. House seat in Vermont since [[Bernie Sanders]] [[2006 United States Senate election in Vermont|ran for the U.S. Senate]] in [[2006 United States House of Representatives election in Vermont|2006]].<ref name="Welch">{{cite web|last=Forgey|first=Quint|title=Rep. Peter Welch launches Senate bid for Leahy's seat|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2021/11/22/peter-welch-senate-campaign-patrick-leahy-seat-523176|access-date=2021-11-22|website=Politico|date=November 22, 2021}}</ref>

Vermont's at-large is generally considered a [[Safe seat|safe]] Democratic seat. If elected, Democratic nominee [[Becca Balint]] will become the first elected female member of the [[United States Congress]] in the state's history, which would make Vermont the last state to elect a woman to Congress. Her primary opponent in the general election, [[Liam Madden]], won the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nomination but identifies as an [[Independent politician|Independent]] who opposes the [[two-party system]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wcax.com/2022/08/10/madden-face-balint-us-house-race/?outputType=amp|title=Madden 'up in the air' about accepting GOP nomination for US House|work=[[WCAX-TV]]|date=9 August 2022|access-date=14 August 2022}}</ref> Madden stated that he would not caucus with House Republicans if elected to Congress; the [[Vermont Republican Party]] later disavowed his campaign.<ref name="MaddenDisavowed">{{Cite web |last=Cutler |first=Calvin |title=Vermont GOP will not support Liam Madden for US House |url=https://www.wcax.com/2022/08/15/vermont-gop-will-not-support-liam-madden-us-house/ |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=WCAX |language=en}}</ref> Ericka Redic, who lost the Republican primary to Madden, will run in the general election as the candidate of the [[Libertarian Party of Vermont]].<ref name="RedicLibertarian">{{Cite web |last=Weinstein |first=Ethan |date=2022-08-11 |title=Ericka Redic, runner-up in Republican primary, running for U.S. House as a Libertarian |url=https://vtdigger.org/2022/08/11/ericka-redic-runner-up-in-republican-primary-running-for-u-s-house-as-a-libertarian/ |access-date=2022-08-17 |website=VTDigger |language=en-US}}</ref>
